en: Success! Homage to the Blessed Lady, the Noble Dhvajāgrakeyūrā.
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the gods of the Thirty-three on the Pāṇḍukambala stone.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, having been defeated and vanquished by the asuras, approached the Blessed One with haste and in great haste.
Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Here, Blessed One, I have been defeated and vanquished by Vemacitrin, the lord of the asuras, and the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three have also been conquered and vanquished.
In this situation, Blessed One, how should we proceed?
The Blessed One said:

"O Lord of Gods, take up the Aparājitā, who bears the name Dhvajāgrakeyūrā, whom I previously took up when I was a Bodhisattva in the presence of the Tathāgata Aparājitadhvaja; having taken her up, I have extensively proclaimed her to others.
Since that time, I do not recall ever experiencing fear, paralysis, or even the sign of horripilation, nor even a momentary bodily affliction."
"Then, Blessed One, what is this dhāraṇī called Dhvajāgrakeyūrā, the Unconquered?

It is as follows: Oṃ jaya jaya vijaya vijaya jayavāhini śaṅkari bhayaṅkari prabhañjani! Protect, protect Āvadhūtaśrī-Ālakhavajra together with his retinue and all sentient beings! Whether it be an adversary or an enemy who attacks..."
Oṃ! Paralyze, paralyze! Immobilize, immobilize! Delude, delude! O Blessed One, Jayavāhinī!

Crush, crush! Grind, grind! Devour, devour! Laugh, laugh! Hūṃ hūṃ! Lambha lambha! O Lambodarī, three-eyed one, four-faced one, four-fanged one, four-armed one, bearer of the sword, club, discus, trident, vajra, and armor mudrās! Protect, protect the venerable Ālakhavajra, who has shaken off all defilements!

[Protect] all sentient beings, together with their retinues, O Blessed One, from all calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions! He he, Blessed One! Strike, strike! Burn, burn! Cook, cook! Grind, grind! Crush, crush! Completely crush, completely crush! Shake, shake! Completely shake, completely shake! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ! Shatter, shatter the enemy army! Destroy [the obstacles] of Āvadhūtaśrī-Ālakhavajra!
[Protect] all the enemies of [me], together with my retinue! O *dhvajāgrakeyūrā*, *tṛṭa tṛṭa tṛṭu tṛṭu*, O bearer of the torch, O shaker of the three worlds, destroy the enemy army!
Protect, protect Āvadhūtaśrī-Ālakhavajra, together with his retinue and all sentient beings, from all calamities!

Move! Move! Cili cili! Culu culu! Kala kala! Kili kili! Kulu kulu! Abandon your fierce, loud laughter! Destroy the enemy army! Terrify it! Terrify it! Baffle it! Baffle it! By the truth of the Buddha, by the truth of the Dharma, by the truth of the Saṅgha, and by the truth of those who speak the truth!
Do not transgress the truth of the Buddha!
Do not transgress the truth of the Dharma; do not transgress the truth of the Saṅgha;
do not transgress the truth of those who speak the truth.
O Lambodarī! Kuṭa kuṭa, kuṭṭa kuṭṭa! Bring Rudra!
Bring Viṣṇu!
Bring the Moon and the Sun!
Bring the Lord of the Three Worlds!
Bring the Lord of all Devas!
Bring all the Devas!
Bring all the yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, mahoragas, and nāgas!
Destroy the enemy army!
Raṅga raṅga raṅgāpaya raṅgāpaya jvala jvala puṣpamālini rundha rundha riṭi riṭi ciṭi!
Ciṭi! O you with the frowning face, who causes the enemy army to tremble; hala hala, hili hili, hulu hulu, hūṃ hūṃ, he he, riṇi riṇi, O you who crush the pride of the enemy!
O you who look upon the Buddhas on the banner, protect, protect Āvadhūtaśrī Āla-khavajra together with his retinue and all sentient beings, O you who look upon all the Tathāgatas, svāhā!
Svāhā to the Radiance of the King of Qualities!
Svāhā to the Immaculate Sun and Fire! Svāhā to the Immaculate Moon and Fire!
Svāhā! To the darkening of all planets and constellations, svāhā! Hūṃ hūṃ! Protect, protect Āvadhūta Śrī Ālakhavajra, together with his retinue and all sentient beings, from all fears, svāhā!
O Lord of Devas, this is that Aparājitā Dhāraṇī named Dhvajāgrakeyūrā.
Wherever one may go—in battle, in strife, in conflict, or in dispute—there shall be victory everywhere.
When bound to the top of a banner or worn around the neck, it should be maintained by a king of men; it provides protection for all heroic men.
Assuming the form of a woman, she stands before one;
she grants fearlessness, provides protection, and puts to flight the enemy army.
She is auspicious, pure, and the establisher of Śrī Lakṣmī.
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
With joyful minds, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and those monks and those bodhisattvas rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
The Dhāraṇī named Āryadhvajāgrakeyūrā is completed.
Oṃ, Blessed One, you who possess armlets at the tip of the banner, you who destroy the enemy armies,
you who protect one’s own army,
O Ulkāmukhī!
Kha kha! Khāhi khāhi!
Strike, strike the enemy army with infinite mouths and infinite arms!
Hūṃ hūṃ / Phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.
The Heart of the Noble Crest-Jewel at the Tip of the Banner is completed.
